bullets.title: Semis now 14% of market cap, nearly 2x dot-com peak—structural concentration risk elevated
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag that the semiconductor sector now represents 14% of total US market capitalization, versus roughly 8% at the dot-com bubble peak. Separately, the SOX index is down 17% month-to-date while the broadest semiconductor names remain 10%+ below their 50-day moving averages, with analysts suggesting a bottom formation attempt but no confirmation yet.

bullets.title: Hedge funds cutting tech at record pace—largest sector outflow on record per Goldman
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs data shows hedge funds have been net sellers of tech for 6 of the past 8 weeks, reducing sector exposure by roughly 10%. This is described as the largest tech sector outflow since the data series began over a decade ago, even as the S&P 500 opened Monday up ~0.54%.

bullets.title: S&P 500 earnings beat rate at 92%—well above historical norms
bullets.body: With a large share of companies having reported, 92% of S&P 500 firms beat earnings estimates this season, a notably elevated beat rate versus the typical ~79% one-year average.

bullets.title: 10Y Treasury yield back at 4.60%; UK 30Y gilts hit 5.75%—rates ripping higher
bullets.body: The 10-year US Treasury yield returned to 4.60%, signaling persistent macro uncertainty. UK 30-year gilt yields rose more than 8bps to 5.749%, the highest since May 20, driven by new PM Burnham's comments invoking 'flexibility' within existing fiscal rules—causing Alphabet's 100-year sterling bond to lose 7%+ since its February issuance.

bullets.title: Conference Board LEI -0.2% in June, misses -0.1% estimate—macro momentum softening
bullets.body: The Conference Board Leading Economic Index fell 0.2% month-over-month in June, worse than the -0.1% economist consensus and reversing the prior month's +0.1% gain. The miss reinforces concerns about decelerating US economic momentum heading into H2.

bullets.title: Fed enters blackout window; July FOMC holds near-certain at ~95% probability
bullets.body: The Federal Reserve entered its pre-FOMC blackout window Monday, cutting off official commentary ahead of next week's meeting. Market pricing implies roughly 95% probability of no rate action in July, though former NY Fed President Dudley suggested tightening pressure could build by fall.

bullets.title: US-Iran military escalation: strikes reported, oil/energy assets repricing
bullets.body: Reports of US airstrikes on Shiraz and other Iranian-linked targets, Iranian Revolutionary Guard claims of targeting Gulf military bases in Bahrain and Kuwait, tankers struck near the Strait of Hormuz, and the US preparing a 'next phase' military campaign. Heating oil prices approached Iran-war highs. Iran later signaled openness to negotiations, causing oil to erase gains. US Strategic Petroleum Reserve at its lowest since 1983 (~311.4mb, down 5.1mb w/w), amplifying energy price sensitivity.

bullets.title: Post-OpEx: market lost its volatility shock absorber; negative SPY gamma with $2.3B put wall at 740
bullets.body: With options expiration behind it, the market has shed its structural hedging cushion. SPY gamma remains negative into the week with a $2.3 billion put wall at the 740 strike, while large OTM SPY/QQQ puts were detected. Separately, $10M+ in SOXX call LEAPS also appeared, suggesting bifurcated positioning.

bullets.title: AI capex sustainability questioned: Goldman flags 'couple of weeks' from bottom; $5.3T hyperscaler spend eyes bond markets
bullets.body: Goldman's One-Delta desk publicly questioned AI capex sustainability and suggested the market is 'still a couple of weeks away from a bottom.' Separately, Goldman estimated that $5.3 trillion in AI spending by Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet through 2030 could pressure bond markets. The AI unwind was characterized by multiple sources as leverage-, options-, and dealer-hedging-driven rather than earnings-specific.

bullets.title: US closed-source AI costs 50-100x Chinese open-weight alternatives—competitive pressure intensifying
bullets.body: Chamath and multiple sources quantify the AI pricing fork: closed-source US models run $26-56 per million tokens while Chinese open-weight alternatives (Qwen3.8, DeepSeek V4) cost $0.50-1 per million tokens. Chamath additionally called token-based scaling a 'bridge to nowhere,' while Ramp reported a 21x surge in enterprise token spend over 12 months, underscoring the adoption trajectory.

bullets.title: AMD-Microsoft expand strategic AI partnership: Helios Rackscale on Azure for frontier inference
bullets.body: AMD and Microsoft announced an expanded strategic partnership, with Microsoft deploying AMD's Helios Rackscale solution—combining MI455X GPUs, EPYC Venice CPUs, Pensando DPUs, and ROCm software—at scale on Azure for frontier model inference. This marks AMD's 2H26 inflection as OpenAI begins ramping its first 1GW of MI450 deployment.

bullets.title: Google 'Frozen V2' custom AI chip targets 6-10x tokens-per-watt efficiency, deployment by 2028
bullets.body: Google is developing its Frozen V2 chip, which embeds the Gemini architecture directly into silicon to reduce data movement and compute requirements, projecting 6-10x more tokens per unit of power than competitors. Deployment is targeted as early as 2028, with a follow-on chip planned further out—reinforcing Google's push to reduce third-party silicon dependence.

bullets.title: Micron crosses $1T market cap; ADATA warns DRAM shortage persists 10 more years
bullets.body: Micron's market cap crossed back above $1 trillion Monday. ADATA's chairman warned the DRAM shortage will last another decade, calling electricity and memory the world's scarcest resources going forward. ASML's memory revenue share has surged above 60% of trailing systems revenue, up from ~35% in late 2023, corroborating the structural demand view.

bullets.title: IREN surges ~20% on $2.8B AI cloud contract wins, raising ARR target to $4B+
bullets.body: IREN signed $2.8 billion in new multi-year AI cloud services contracts with customers including Microsoft, Nvidia, Perplexity, and Figure, raising its year-end 2026 ARR guidance to $4B+. The company is also securing 45% prepayments on new contracts—a bullish signal for the neocloud sector broadly—driving its stock up roughly 19.7% on the day.

bullets.title: Meta monetizing surplus GPU capacity via Anthropic compute lease—new cloud revenue stream
bullets.body: Meta is converting excess AI infrastructure capacity into a cloud business by leasing compute to Anthropic. The move diversifies Meta's revenue base and signals that hyperscaler overbuilding may be finding commercial outlets beyond internal use.

bullets.title: Paramount-WBD merger halted by federal judge; 14-day TRO issued ahead of injunction battle
bullets.body: A federal judge issued a temporary restraining order halting Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, with a ruling expected around July 22. Legal commentary highlights a contradiction between Paramount's pitch to Wall Street on distributor leverage and its denial of that same leverage in court filings.

bullets.title: US large-company bankruptcies hit 16-year high at 372 in H1 2026
bullets.body: The US recorded 372 large-company bankruptcies in the first half of 2026, the highest first-half total in 16 years and the fourth consecutive year-over-year increase for the period—consistent with tight credit conditions and the impact of sustained above-neutral rates.

bullets.title: Canada CPI cools sharply to 2.8% YoY in June—disinflation broadening across advanced economies
bullets.body: Canada's June CPI fell 0.4% month-over-month (vs. -0.2% expected) and slowed to 2.8% year-over-year from 3.2% in May. Core measures also beat estimates. The print extends a string of softer-than-expected inflation readings across advanced economies, though geopolitical escalation (Iran, Hormuz) poses an upside risk to energy prices.

bullets.title: BlackRock issuing $12B+ in bonds to finance El Paso data center campus
bullets.body: BlackRock is marketing more than $12 billion in bonds to fund a large data center campus in El Paso, Texas—reflecting the continued capital market appetite for AI infrastructure financing at scale.

bullets.title: Barclays upgrades Lumentum to Overweight on AI networking and optical components demand
bullets.body: Barclays upgraded LITE to Overweight ahead of chip earnings, citing greater confidence in AI networking component demand and stronger optical components fundamentals. The call is consistent with the broader neocloud and AI infrastructure buildout theme driving the week's sector moves.
